title: Electron transfer reactions
summary: Redox reactions transfer electrons. Use oxidation states and half-equations, compare metal reactivity, and explain voltaic and electrolytic cells; at HL, standard electrode potentials, E⦵ and ΔG, and electrolysis of aqueous solutions.

keyterms.definition: Loss of electrons, or an increase in oxidation state.
Gain of electrons, or a decrease in oxidation state.
A species that causes oxidation by accepting electrons; it is itself reduced.
A species that causes reduction by donating electrons; it is itself oxidized.
An equation showing either the oxidation or the reduction part of a redox reaction, with electrons.
Metals ranked by how readily they are oxidized; a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from solution.
Converts chemical energy from a spontaneous redox reaction into electrical energy.
Uses electrical energy to drive a non-spontaneous redox reaction.
The electrode where oxidation occurs (negative in a voltaic cell, positive in an electrolytic cell).
The electrode where reduction occurs (positive in a voltaic cell, negative in an electrolytic cell).
Connects half-cells, allowing ions to move to balance charge while keeping solutions separate.
Potential of a half-cell relative to the standard hydrogen electrode (0 V) under standard conditions.
Reference half-cell: Pt in 1 mol dm⁻³ H⁺ with H₂ gas at 100 kPa, 298 K; assigned E⦵ = 0.00 V.
Electrolysis that deposits a thin layer of metal on an object made the cathode.

questions.prompt: In Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, which species is oxidized?
questions.explanation: Zn loses two electrons (0 → +2).

questions.text: A species that is reduced is acting as the ___ agent.
questions.explanation: By accepting electrons it oxidizes the other species.

questions.statement: In 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, oxygen is the reducing agent.
questions.explanation: O goes from 0 to −2, so it is reduced: oxygen is the oxidizing agent; Mg is the reducing agent.
Mn: +7 → +2 gains 5 electrons; check charge: −1 + 8 − 5 = +2.

questions.prompt: Match each process to its definition.
questions.explanation: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain.

questions.prompt: Which metal will displace copper from copper(II) sulfate solution?
questions.explanation: Iron is above copper in the activity series, so it is more easily oxidized.

questions.prompt: Order these metals by reactivity, most reactive first.
questions.explanation: More reactive metals lose electrons more readily.

questions.text: Ethanol is oxidized to ethanoic acid by acidified potassium ___.
questions.explanation: Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) is reduced to Cr³⁺ (green) under reflux.

questions.statement: Primary alcohols can be oxidized to aldehydes and then carboxylic acids.
questions.explanation: Distil off the aldehyde to stop at that stage; reflux for the acid. Tertiary alcohols are not oxidized easily.

questions.prompt: Which reacts with dilute HCl to produce hydrogen?
questions.explanation: Metals above hydrogen in the activity series reduce H⁺ to H₂.

questions.prompt: In a Zn/Cu voltaic cell, electrons flow through the external circuit…
questions.explanation: Zn is oxidized (anode, negative) and its electrons flow to Cu (cathode).

questions.statement: In both types of cell, oxidation occurs at the anode.
questions.explanation: An Ox, Red Cat applies to voltaic and electrolytic cells; only the polarity differs.

questions.text: The purpose of the salt bridge is to allow the movement of ___ to balance charge.
questions.explanation: Electrons flow in the wire; ions flow through the bridge.

questions.prompt: In the electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide, what forms at the cathode?
questions.explanation: Pb²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Pb at the negative cathode; Br₂ forms at the anode.
Voltaic reactions are spontaneous; electrolysis needs an external supply.

questions.statement: Solid sodium chloride can be electrolysed.
questions.explanation: Ions must be mobile, so the electrolyte must be molten or in solution.

questions.text: In the electrolysis of molten NaCl, the half-equation at the anode is 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2___.
questions.explanation: Chloride ions lose electrons (oxidation) at the positive anode.

questions.prompt: Order the events in a Zn/Cu voltaic cell.
items: Zn atoms lose electrons at the anode
Cu²⁺ ions gain electrons at the cathode
Ions move through the salt bridge to balance charge
questions.explanation: A complete circuit needs both electron flow and ion flow.

questions.prompt: Which change increases the voltage of a Mg/Cu cell compared with a Zn/Cu cell?
options: Mg is more reactive than Zn, so there is a bigger difference in reactivity
questions.explanation: A larger difference in reducing power gives a larger cell potential.

questions.prompt: A secondary (rechargeable) cell differs from a primary cell because…
options: its reaction can be reversed by applying a current
questions.explanation: e.g. lithium-ion and lead–acid batteries can be recharged; primary cells cannot.

questions.prompt: E⦵(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, E⦵(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V. E⦵cell for the Zn/Cu cell is…
questions.explanation: E⦵cell = E⦵(cathode) − E⦵(anode) = 0.34 − (−0.76) = +1.10 V.

questions.statement: A positive E⦵cell means the reaction is spontaneous.
questions.explanation: ΔG⦵ = −nFE⦵, so positive E⦵ gives negative ΔG⦵.

questions.text: The standard hydrogen electrode is assigned an E⦵ of ___ V.
questions.explanation: All other potentials are measured relative to it.

questions.prompt: Which is the strongest oxidizing agent? E⦵: F₂/F⁻ +2.87, Cl₂/Cl⁻ +1.36, Br₂/Br⁻ +1.07, I₂/I⁻ +0.54 V
questions.explanation: The most positive E⦵ means the species is most easily reduced.

questions.text: For a cell with n = 2 and E⦵ = +1.10 V, ΔG⦵ = −nFE⦵ ≈ ___ kJ mol⁻¹ (F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹).

questions.prompt: Electrolysis of concentrated NaCl(aq): match the electrode to its product.
questions.explanation: Water is reduced rather than Na⁺; high [Cl⁻] makes Cl₂ form at the anode.

questions.statement: In the electrolysis of dilute aqueous sodium sulfate, oxygen forms at the anode.
questions.explanation: SO₄²⁻ is very hard to oxidize, so water is oxidized: 2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻.

questions.prompt: To copper-plate an iron key, the key should be…
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ is reduced and deposited at the cathode; a copper anode replenishes Cu²⁺.

questions.prompt: Order the components of the standard hydrogen electrode description.
questions.explanation: Platinum is inert and provides a surface for H₂ ⇌ 2H⁺ + 2e⁻.

questions.prompt: Which factor does NOT affect the product formed at an electrode in aqueous electrolysis?
questions.explanation: Position in the E⦵ series, concentration and the electrode material all matter.
